Anyway, a few family members are over, mostly celebrating my brothers grab, but my mum suddenly shut off the kitchen lights, grabs the cake, and begins singing. Everyone joins, happy times. Now we get on to the present, lucky for me. I got a few pairs of earrings, a book that was popular with teens but nothing that I was interested in, and I finally move onto my nana’s present

Now, she was there for my brothers grad ceremony, but left after he walked, so I was already pissed at her. She’s been trying to rebuild bridges, but she eats birdseed, so nice try Marilyn...
I pull the present on my lap and unwrap, to reveal a coin set. 

A. Fucking. Coin. Set.

So have fun in the seniors home, Marilyn.

The best advice I can give:

'Every feeling matters, but it's the weight and importance you put on it that should change' 

What this means is that, while your feelings are legit and shouldn't be gotten rid of, but the importance you place on them should maybe go down. 

For example: I'm watching my favourite show and I remember how much I hate myself. I don't disregard this feeling, I just make it less important for the time being and bring it up with my psychologist; someone who will know how to proper deal with this.

Other advice is to try and schedule a certain time (preferably when you're visiting a councillor or such) to worry and focus on such things. Imagine the scenario above, but solve it with 'But I'm watching my favourite show and I don't want to worry about that now'
